openQuestions.text: Cross-phase records: do the phases agree on shared records and their exact shape (by: actor, needs-you grants, operators.json and roles, conversation JSONL, memory files, state-root layout, HonoredPosture fields)? List every conflict between two phases.

Failure modes: what happens across the plans on restarts, lost or duplicated messages and answers, concurrent approvals from the terminal and a chat, prompt injection through memory, skills or chat, and routine until and fatigue edge cases?

Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and CLI verbs each of the eleven phase plans names exist in the built runtime with the shapes the plan assumes, and are the test and verify commands in every tasks.md and acceptance-criteria.md runnable here (vitest paths, cargo for the Rust screen)? List every mismatch.

Security: in the vault (008), apps (007), approvals (006), memory (005) and channels (011) plans, where can secrets leak into prompts, logs, run records or chat, how are tokens stored, and can a spoofed or unlinked chat user approve or read?
Who is allowed to answer a needs-you item, and can a chat sender be linked to the operator before any approval is honored across the 006, 011 and 001 plans?
How is a standing grant listed, revoked or expired once a rule store exists, and what stops an `always` grant from becoming permanent silent authority?
Do the secret scans cover child transcripts and logs written outside the run folder, such as an executor's own session store, or only the run folder the plan scans?

Do the eleven plans agree on the `bots status --json` key set that phase 003's header and phase 004's lastRun fields both extend, and does any phase add a key without updating the terminal screen's parser?

keyFindings.text: **P1 — Phase 001 and phase 004 contradict each other on `SCHEMA_VERSION`, and both modify `status-index.ts`.** Phase 001's plan says the index "gains the `actor` column and a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump" and its verify command expects `SCHEMA_VERSION = '3'` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:60] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:76]. Phase 004's plan instead requires that `SCHEMA_VERSION` "stays `'2'`" and its setup and file-table checks both assert `SCHEMA_VERSION = '2'` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/plan.md:49] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/plan.md:82] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/spec.md:147]. The runtime today holds `'2'` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts:55]. Because 001 lands first, 004's setup step and its verify command fail the moment 001 is built. **Exact edit**: in `004-computer-exposure/plan.md` replace both `SCHEMA_VERSION = '2'` assertions with `SCHEMA_VERSION = '3'` and add the sentence "phase 001 already bumped the index to 3; this phase adds JSON summary fields without a second bump"; alternatively, in `001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:60,76` drop the bump and carry `actor` as a JSON column the way 004 carries `RunSummary` fields.

**P1 — phase 001, `tasks.md:138` (CHK-010): the typecheck verify command is not runnable as written.** `cd .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime && npx tsc --noEmit` cannot resolve a local `tsc`: `runtime/node_modules/.bin` holds `esbuild nanoid prebuild-install rc rolldown semver tsx vite vitest why-is-node-running` and no `tsc`. The repo's own typecheck script is `../../system-spec-kit/node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --composite false -p tsconfig.json`, and that binary exists. `npx tsc` would fetch the unrelated deprecated `tsc` package or fail offline, so CHK-010 either fails or checks the wrong compiler. **Exact edit:** replace the CHK-010 Verify with `cd $RT && npm run typecheck` and add that same command to the phase-001 Definition of Done. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/package.json:13] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts:55]

keyFindings.text: **P1 — the parent spec still describes ten phases while the phase map lists eleven.** The title and description say "Ten build phases" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:3], §3 In Scope says "The ten ranked slices ... one child phase each" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:78], the Files to Change preamble says "the ten phases touch" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:100], and the Handoff Criteria still say "010-conversations closes the program" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:55], while the phase map carries an eleventh row for `011-messaging-channels/` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:131]. 011 itself says it "extends the program rather than continuing its order" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:43]. **Exact edit**: change `spec.md:3` to "Eleven build phases", `spec.md:78` to "The ten ranked slices ... plus the messaging-channels extension", `spec.md:100` to "the eleven phases touch", and `spec.md:55` to "011-messaging-channels closes the program".

**Phase 011-messaging-channels has no row in the 002 ranked build order, so it is net-new scope that the parity research never sized or ranked.** The 002 order has eleven items: activity/actor, routine layer, computer exposure, memory, grants, per-bot apps, vault, skills, conversations, TUI, desktop shell (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:139-158`). Items 1-9 map one-to-one onto phases 001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010; item 10 (TUI) is phase 003; item 11 (desktop) is explicitly out of scope (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:85`). Phase 011 answers none of them. **Severity P1.** Fix: add a twelfth row to the 002 ranked order (or a "post-parity" note in `specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md` §3) that names messaging channels, its size and its risk, and state in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §1 that the phase is post-parity scope rather than a research slice. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:139-158] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:114-143]

**P1 — the parent's Files to Change table omits every 011 surface.** The `bots.cjs` row lists phases "001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:104], the runtime row says "001-010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:105], and the `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row lists "001, 002, 008, 009, 010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:109], yet 011 adds a `bots channel` verb group [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:155], five `channel-*.ts` runtime modules [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:137-140] and Apache-2.0 notices for rakazo and turnstone [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:160]. **Exact edit**: append `011` to the phase column of `spec.md:104`, change `spec.md:105` to "001-011", and append `011` to `spec.md:109`.

**P1 — The terminal screen's "approve always" and "deny" keys cannot express phase 006's scope contract, so both silently record `once`.** Phase 003 binds `a` to answer `always` and `n` to answer `deny` as the answer text [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:166], and its plan says the binary's only write is `bots answer` with no option named [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/plan.md:87] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/plan.md:95]. Phase 006 records the grant scope from `--scope once|conversation|always|deny` and states that "an answer with no `--scope` records `once`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:149]. The result: pressing `a` writes answer text `always` but scope `once`; pressing `n` writes answer text `deny` but scope `once`, so a deny from the screen grants once. **Exact edit**: in `003-terminal-screen/spec.md` REQ-006 and REQ-009, and in `003-terminal-screen/plan.md` at the write path, change the write to `bots answer <id> <text> --scope once|always|deny`, and add a dependency row on 006's `--scope` flag to the plan's dependency table.

**P2 — phase 001, `spec.md:132`, `tasks.md:67` (T025), `acceptance-criteria.md:59` (AC-006): the MIT notice file has no stated location and does not exist anywhere in the repository.** `fd -HI THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` returns nothing, so the file is created by this phase, yet the spec's Files to Change names it as the bare `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and both verify clauses `rg` a bare filename from an unstated working directory. Two implementers can create it at the repo root and under `.skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/` and both "pass" their own check. **Exact edit:** in the spec's Files to Change row, T025 and AC-006, write the exact target path (proposed: `.skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, beside the runtime the lifted files land in) and make each verify `rg -n 'activity-groups.ts|activity-rows.ts' <that path>`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/README.md:1]

keyFindings.text: **Phase 011 builds five transports where the small-team model needs one plus the terminal, which is the largest overbuild in the packet.** The phase adds `channel.ts`, `channel-link.ts`, `channel-approval.ts`, `channel-queue.ts` and five transports — Telegram, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp and terminal — plus six verbs (`bots channel list|link|unlink|send|listen|drain`) (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:111-116`). The 002 small-team model says "the terminal is the client" and the skip list rules out mobile (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:103-116`). WhatsApp additionally needs a public HTTPS URL or tunnel and a Meta business account, which the phase itself lists as an operator prerequisite (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:116`). **Severity P1.** Fix: cut `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3 In Scope to Telegram long polling plus the terminal fallback, move Slack, Signal and WhatsApp into a new `012-messaging-transports` phase, and move `channel-approval.ts` and `channel-queue.ts` into the retained slice only if the Telegram path needs them.

**`operators.json` is a direct parent/child contradiction: the parent forbids any child from building it and phase 011 builds it.** The parent says "The rest of the small-team model (§12): two roles in one `operators.json` and a shared host at mode 0770. No child builds them; 001 lands the actor field alone" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:94`). Phase 001 repeats the deferral (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:100`) and phase 006 repeats it again (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:107`). Phase 011 then decides "yes, the minimal roster" and makes REQ-005 depend on it: "Only an actor named `owner` or listed in `members` in `operators.json`…" (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177`, `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281`). **Severity P0** — 011 cannot meet its own REQ-005 without a file the parent forbids, and no phase owns that file's schema, its write path or its mode. Fix: move `operators.json` ownership into phase 001 (it already owns `actor.ts` and the actor precedence), change `spec.md:94` to "001 lands the actor field and the `operators.json` roster; no other child builds it", and change `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281` to read the roster from 001 instead of landing it.

**P1 — 011 lands `operators.json` while the parent's Out of Scope forbids any child from building it, and 011's justification cites a parent edit that was never made.** The parent says "The rest of the small-team model (§12): two roles in one `operators.json` and a shared host at mode 0770. No child builds them; 001 lands the actor field alone" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:94]. 011 decides "yes, the minimal roster" and asserts "the parent's phase-map row records it" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281], but the 011 phase-map row names only "a file-backed identity link" and the 001/006/008/010 dependencies [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:131]. **Exact edit**: replace `spec.md:94` with "The two-role `operators.json` and the shared-host 0770 mode: 001 lands the actor field alone, and 011 lands the minimal `owner`/`members` roster its approver check needs", and add "the `operators.json` roster" to the 011 row at `spec.md:131`.

**P1 — phase 002, `plan.md:88`: the affected-surface row misstates `status.ts`'s current role, so the task that adds the `completed` row state understates the change.** The row says `status.ts` "Reads the switches to build a row state" and needs only "update: report `completed`". The module imports no switch reader and builds `flags` from retired/path state, `checkInstalls` status, an open needs-you item, launchd presence and the last index row; `BOT_ROW_STATES` contains no `completed`. The work is therefore a new switch read plus a new state in the precedence list, not a reporting tweak. **Exact edit:** change the row's Current Role to "Reads install checks, path state, launchd, the last index row and open needs-you items; does not read switches", and add to T019: "import `readSwitch` and insert `completed` into `BOT_ROW_STATES` after `held`". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status.ts:41-52] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status.ts:270-282]

keyFindings.text: **P1 — The parent scope statement and phase 011 disagree about who builds `operators.json`.** The parent says "The rest of the small-team model (§12): two roles in one `operators.json` and a shared host at mode 0770. No child builds them; 001 lands the actor field alone" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:94]. Phase 011 lists "the `operators.json` roster" as a deliverable, adds it to `channel-link.ts`, and makes REQ-005 depend on `owner` or `members` in it [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:59] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:133] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177]. Phase 011 documents the deviation in its own decisions section [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281], so the two docs knowingly contradict each other. **Exact edit**: replace `spec.md:94` with "No child builds the shared-host 0770 mode; phase 011 lands the minimal two-role `operators.json` roster its channel approver check needs, and 001 lands the actor field alone", and add `operators.json` to the phase-map row 11 cell that currently lists only 001, 006, 008 and 010.

**P1 — `operators.json` has no write path in any phase.** Phase 011 lands the roster and makes it the sole authority for channel approvals, but its verb list is `bots channel list|link|unlink|send|listen|drain` — none of them adds or removes a roster member [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:59]. `bots channel link` writes the link record, not the roster, and the spec names no path, format or creation rule for the file. A second operator therefore cannot be added through any documented surface, and REQ-005's `members` list is unreachable for a real team. **Exact edit**: add a `bots channel roster add <actor> [--role owner|member]` and `bots channel roster remove <actor>` pair to phase 011's in-scope list and file table, with the roster at `<stateRoot>/<identity>/operators.json`; or, if the roster is intentionally hand-edited, name the exact path, the JSON shape and the creation rule in REQ-005 and add an acceptance criterion that a hand-written roster admits a second member.

**P1 — three phases define three incompatible grammars for answering one needs-you item.** 003 answers through `bots answer` with free text and binds `y` to `approve`, `a` to `always`, `n` to `deny` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:171], and its overlay draws `1 approve once`, `2 approve always`, `n deny` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:174]. 006 adds `bots answer --scope once|conversation|always|deny` and records the scope on the grant [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:96]. 011 sends "the item's `options`, which the runner fills from the `[OPTION]` lines" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:179]. The runtime does carry `options: string[] | null` on the item [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:38] and the marker exists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/dispatch.ts:45], so 011's path is buildable; 003's is not, because `bots answer` accepts no options at all today [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:73]. Consequences: 003's "approve always" records no standing allow, and 006's `conversation` scope has no surface anywhere. **Exact edit**: add to 003 REQ-003 "the write is `bots answer <item-id> <text> --scope <once|always|deny>`", rewrite 003 REQ-006/REQ-009 to the four scopes, and add to 011 REQ-007 "a chosen option maps to the scope 006 names, and an item with no options gets `once`/`deny`".

**P2 — phase 001, `plan.md:140`: the rollback claim about a post-revert record is wrong.** It says a record carrying `actor` "reads as an unknown key only if the revert lands after a run wrote one, and `bots status --rebuild` then skips that record and names it". `validateRunRecord` checks only the eight required groups and a fixed set of nested fields; it rejects neither unknown top-level keys nor unknown keys inside a group, so a reverted reader ignores `actor` and the record is not skipped. **Exact edit:** reword the rollback to "the reverted reader ignores the extra field, so the record still reads and rebuilds". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/run-record.ts:234-248]

keyFindings.text: **The small-team authority check is a parity gap: after all eleven phases, `bots answer` still never checks who may answer.** The 002 model specifies "Two roles. An `owner` (who installed the jobs) and `member`, in one `operators.json` under the state root, checked by `bots answer` before it writes" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:103`). Phase 001 defers the roster (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:100`), phase 006 defers it (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:107`), and phase 011 builds a roster only to gate channel senders (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177`). No phase adds the check to `answer.ts`. **Severity P1.** Fix: add one requirement to `006-approval-grants/spec.md` §4 — "`bots answer` refuses with `actor-not-permitted` when the resolved actor is neither `owner` nor in `members` of `operators.json`" — and one acceptance row for it.

**P1 — the build order puts the approval overlay (003) before the grant vocabulary (006) and no phase revisits it.** 003 is phase 3 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:123] and 006 is phase 6 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:126]. 010 is the only later phase that edits the crate, and it edits `cli.rs` for chat only [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:120]. So the screen's approval path is frozen at pre-006 semantics. **Exact edit**: add a 006 task "Update `crates/bots-tui/src/render/overlay.rs` and `keys.rs` to the four scopes and the `--scope` write", and add `crates/bots-tui` to 006's Files to Change table.

**P2 — The bot-message `by` field is unspecified.** Phase 010 requires every message to carry `by` and says "A human message carries the addressed bot's id and the actor; a bot message carries the replying bot's id and the run id" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:150]. For a bot message the sentence names `botId` and `runId` but never says what `by` holds, so two implementers can write `null`, the bot id, or `bot:<id>` and both satisfy the text. Phase 001 defines `by` as the answer's actor and `actor` as the run record's field [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:146] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:147], which gives no bot-message rule either. **Exact edit**: in `010-conversations/spec.md` REQ-003 add "a bot message carries `by: null` and a human message carries `by: <actor>`", or name `bot:<id>` if that is intended, and mirror the choice in the acceptance criteria.

**Phase 011 duplicates phase 006's approval surface with a second, parallel approval index.** 011 adds `channel-approval.ts`, "a file-backed `approval-v1:<item-id>:<index>` index and the numbered or YES/NO reply grammar, so a restart loses no prompt" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:112`), while 006 already owns `grants` on the needs-you item and the precedence ladder at that gate (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:105-110`). Two indexes mean two answers can be recorded for one item, and the grant scope 006 writes is not what 011 reads. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3, replace the parallel index with "the channel reads the needs-you item id from the delivery entry and writes the answer through `bots answer --scope`, reusing 006's grant"; keep only a restart-safe `sent-prompt` marker, not an approval index.

**P1 — `bots activity --json`'s row shape is never specified by its producer, but its consumer parses six status values out of it.** 001's REQ-002 promises only "each group carrying its id, its title and its rows" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:144], and its acceptance criterion repeats the same three fields [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/acceptance-criteria.md:55]. 003 draws "each with one of six markers: `·` running, `✓` done, `✗` failed, `!` needs input, `–` cancelled, `?` stale" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:168] and its AC-005 asserts a done row carries `✓` and `done` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/acceptance-criteria.md:43]. Nothing names the row's `state`, `botId`, `at` or `actor` fields. **Exact edit**: extend 001 REQ-002 to "each row carrying `botId`, `identity`, `state`, `at`, `actor` and `runId`", and add the same list to AC-002.

**P2 — Phase numbering metadata stops at ten while an eleventh phase exists.** Phases 001 through 010 all declare `Phase N of 10`, and phase 010 declares `Successor | None` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:28] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:30], while phase 011 declares `11 of 11` and `Predecessor | 010-conversations` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:32] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:33]. The parent phase map already carries eleven rows, the last being `011-messaging-channels` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:131]. Phase 007 adds `apps` and says to record `[]` when the bot declares none (`007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:100`); phase 008 adds `secretsUsed` (`008-vault/spec.md:98`). Neither mentions the version, so a record written before 007 has no `apps` and reads identically to a bot that declared none. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `007-per-bot-apps/spec.md` §4, bump `schemaVersion` to `2` and make `validateRunRecord` accept `1` and `2`, treating a missing `apps` on a version-1 record as `null` (unknown) rather than `[]`; have `008-vault/spec.md` add `secretsUsed` under the same version.

**Five phases modify `state-root.ts`, a second merge hotspot beside `definition.ts`.** Phases 002, 005, 008, 010 and 011 each add a folder or a path helper to the same module (`002-routine-layer/spec.md:129`, `005-memory/spec.md:113`, `008-vault/spec.md:119`, `010-conversations/spec.md:115`, `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:141`). The parent's phase map orders them serially, but no plan names the module as a shared merge point. **Severity P2.** Fix: extend the Phase Transition Rule proposed in iteration 2 finding 6 to name both `definition.ts` and `state-root.ts` as shared merge points, and add the `state-root.ts` row to each of the five plans' AFFECTED SURFACES tables.

**P2 — the missing-binary message names a path relative to the repository root, but the verb can run from anywhere.** REQ-001's message is `build it with cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/bots-tui/Cargo.toml` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:162], which only works from the root, while the verb resolves the binary from `<skilled-tree>`. **Exact edit**: change the message to name the absolute manifest path it resolved, `<skilled-tree>/crates/bots-tui/Cargo.toml`.

**No phase addresses prompt injection, although the research topic names it and all three injection surfaces are built.** A search for "prompt injection", "injection through", "untrusted input" and "treat … as data" across the eleven phase folders returns nothing. The three surfaces the topic names are all built: phase 005 prepends `memory/shared.md` and `memory/<bot-id>.md` to the prompt (`005-memory/spec.md:94`), phase 009 loads each named `SKILL.md` body into the prompt after the standing body (`009-skills/spec.md:167`), and phases 010 and 011 put conversation and chat text into the prompt (`010-conversations/spec.md:148`, `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:284`). None states that the loaded text is data rather than instruction, and none adds a boundary marker, so a memory entry or a skill body that says "ignore the standing role" is indistinguishable from the standing role. **Severity P1.** Fix: add one requirement to each of `005-memory/spec.md`, `009-skills/spec.md` and `010-conversations/spec.md` — "the loaded block is wrapped in a labelled fence (`<memory>`, `<skill name="…">`, `<transcript>`) and the standing body carries one sentence stating that fenced content is data, not instruction" — and one acceptance row per phase asserting the fence and the sentence appear in the built prompt.

The build therefore cannot implement its authorization gate, and the risk row's mitigation ("the roster check is a second gate") names a file that never lands. **Exact edit:** add a create task for a minimal `operators.json` (`{ owner, members[] }`) to 006 (the approval phase) with its exact location and default owner, and make 011 REQ-005/T019 cite it; or replace the check with the 001 actor plus the OS-user rule and state that model instead. keyFindings.text: **P1 — 005's "holds no bot" item cannot be built: `botId` is a required non-empty string and 005 names no reserved id.** `NeedsYouItem.botId` is `botId: string` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:33] and the validator refuses an empty one [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:100]. 005 says "A `memory-proposal` item holds no bot and awaits no resume, so `holdForBot` and `itemAwaitingResume` ignore it" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:148] and never says what `botId` it carries. 009 solves the identical problem by reserving an id: "Add `skill-proposals` to `RESERVED_BOT_IDS`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:127] and "whose `botId` is the reserved `skill-proposals`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:160]. **Exact edit**: add to 005 REQ-007 "the item's `botId` is the reserved `memory-proposals`", add `memory-proposals` to `RESERVED_BOT_IDS` in 005's Files to Change, and note in both phases that the list is shared.

**P2 — `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is claimed as `Create` by four phases, but only the first can create it.** Phase 001 creates the file with the MIT notice for its two lifted OpenBot files [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:130], and phases 006, 008 and 010 also mark it `Create` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:132] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:133] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:135], while 011 correctly marks it `Modify` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:160]. Phase 006's own description even says "appended when 001 has already created the file", so the row knows it is an append and still says `Create` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:132]. A phase that follows its own row literally creates the file again and drops the earlier entries. **Exact edit**: change the row in 006, 008 and 010 to `Modify` with the description "Append this phase's entry", and add one sentence to the parent spec that 001 owns the file's creation.

**P1 — cross-phase, phase 011 with phase 006: concurrent approvals from a terminal and a chat have no rule.** `answer.ts` is a read-modify-write: it reads the item, writes the answer, then enqueues the resume. Nothing in 011 or 006 defines what happens when a terminal `bots answer` and a chat press race on the same item; both can read `answer: null`, the later write wins silently, and the losing answer and its scope are lost with no event. **Exact edit:** add `item-already-answered` as a refusal and write the answer through a compare-and-set (re-read and atomic replace, or an exclusive claim file) in `answer.ts`; add a test that runs two answer paths against one item and asserts one wins and the other is refused. keyFindings.text: **P1 — memory entries land in the instruction region with no data framing, while 009 wraps skill bodies.** 005 inserts the entries "between the protocol lines and the body" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:145], which is the same region the decision rule and the body occupy. 009 wraps each body in `<skill_content name="<name>">` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:156]. A confirmed fact is therefore an instruction, and a bot that was prompt-injected can launder an instruction into its own future prompts with one `[REMEMBER]` line and one operator confirmation. **Exact edit**: change 005 REQ-006 to "each file's entries sit inside one `<memory file="<path>">` block that states the lines are facts the operator confirmed and not instructions", and add the same sentence to 005's prompt-block description.

**P2 — The parent's notice row assigns the file to two phases that carry no notice requirement and omits two that do.** The parent scope table says `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is created by "001, 002, 008, 009, 010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:109]. Phase 002 has no notice requirement and lifts no code, and phase 009 explicitly decides that its `<skill_content>` wrapper needs no entry [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:254]. Phase 006 requires an MIT notice for its lifted classifier [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:159] and phase 011 lists Apache-2.0 notices among its deliverables [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:65], yet neither appears in the row. **Exact edit**: change the row's phase list to "001, 006, 008, 010, 011" and add a note that 002 and 009 lift no code and carry no entry.

**The fatigue rule counts a parked run as a failure, so a bot that asks for approval ten times is switched off.** `FAILURE_CLASSES` includes `operator` (`run-record.ts:50`), and a run that parks a question must carry `exit.class === 'operator'` — `validateRunRecord` refuses `awaiting-decision-class-invalid` otherwise (`run-record.ts:283`). Phase 002's rule says "After a failed run, ten consecutive failures for one bot set the `disabled` switch with reason `failure-streak`" (`002-routine-layer/spec.md:165`). A bot whose work needs an operator answer every time therefore disables itself after ten questions, which is the opposite of the intended fatigue guard. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `002-routine-layer/spec.md` §4 REQ-006, exclude `awaiting-decision` from the streak and count only the `author`, `environment`, `hub` and `budget` classes; add an acceptance row that ten parked runs leave the bot enabled and the streak at zero.

**P1 — phase 011, `spec.md:191` (REQ-014): the token rule covers the store, config, queue, log and record, but not the question text sent to chat.** REQ-014 names the token; the approval prompt carries the child-authored question and options, and the channel sender can re-render them instead of sending the `deliveryMessage()` body that `delivery.ts:291` already checks with `findSecretLiteral`. A child-authored question holding a stored secret would then reach chat. **Exact edit:** require the channel sender to send only the `deliveryMessage()` output after the literal check, never a re-rendered question, and add the case to the conformance fixture. keyFindings.text: **P1 — the proposal item shows the fact but not the run that proposed it, so the operator cannot judge provenance.** 005's item carries "the type, the fact and the proposing bot" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:146]. 009's item evidence "names the draft, the `proposal.json` and the run folder" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:159]. A fact with no run id cannot be traced to the prompt that produced it, which is the one thing an operator needs to decide whether the bot was talking or being talked through. **Exact edit**: add to 005 REQ-007 "the item's evidence names the run id and the run folder".

**The needs-you item is extended by three phases, two of them add a field called `kind`, and the item's key allowlist is closed.** `ITEM_KEYS` rejects any unknown key with `unknown-key` (`needs-you.ts:51-98`). Phase 001 adds `by` to the answer (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:146`), phase 005 adds `kind` and `proposal` to the item (`005-memory/spec.md:116`), and phase 006 adds `grants`, which itself carries an action `kind` (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:94`). The three must land in one order and agree on one key set, and the two `kind`s mean different things. **Severity P1.** Fix: add a Phase Transition Rule naming `needs-you.ts`'s `ITEM_KEYS` as a shared merge point beside `definition.ts` and `state-root.ts`, and rename phase 005's top-level `kind` to `itemKind` so it cannot be read as the action kind.

**Verified — no forward file dependency exists.** Every `Modify` path that is missing today is created by an earlier phase: `crates/bots-tui/*` is created by 003 and modified by 010, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is created by 001 and modified by 011. No phase modifies a file that only a later phase creates.

**A memory proposal shows the fact but not its provenance, so an operator confirms attacker-authored text without seeing where it came from.** Phase 005 turns a bot's `[REMEMBER] <type> <fact>` line into a `memory-proposal` item (`005-memory/spec.md:96`) whose fields are `kind` and `proposal` (`005-memory/spec.md:116`). The stored entry carries `actor`, `source` and `date` (`005-memory/spec.md:94`), but the proposal item does not carry the source, so the confirmation screen shows the fact alone. A bot that read a hostile file or page can therefore get its text into shared memory with one operator click. **Severity P1.** Fix: add `source` to the `proposal` object — the run id plus the file or URL the fact came from — and require `bots inbox` to print it on the proposal line.

**P2 — no phase strips control characters from a question, a fact or a skill body before it is stored or drawn.** 003's inbox pane draws the item's question [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:169] and `bots inbox` prints it, so a fact carrying a terminal escape sequence can rewrite the screen an operator is approving from. **Exact edit**: add to 005 and 009 "the text is stripped of C0 control characters other than newline and tab before it is stored, and the same strip runs before any text is drawn".

**P2 — phase 011, `spec.md:175` (REQ-003): the pairing code's shape is unspecified.** A one-time code with a 5-failure/300 s lockout is only as strong as its entropy, and REQ-003 never states the length, alphabet, expiry or whether the code is bound to the channel and actor that generated it. **Exact edit:** state the code's length and alphabet (proposed: 8 characters from a 32-symbol unambiguous alphabet), its expiry (10 minutes), and that it is bound to the generating channel and actor. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:175]

keyFindings.text: **Phase 011 creates a `seen/` folder and no requirement says what it holds, so a message body could land there unchecked.** `state-root.ts` gains `channelFolder` and `ensureChannelState`, "naming `channels/` and its `queue/` and `seen/` folders" (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:141`), and the dedupe decision needs only the message id as the event id (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:284`). The phases that actually carry a notice task are 001 (T025), 006 (T031), 008 (T015), 010 (T027) and 011 (T043) [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/tasks.md:67] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/tasks.md:73] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/tasks.md:64] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/tasks.md:69] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/tasks.md:86]. **P2 — Phase 011 builds five transports in one phase, where the research ranks no messaging slice and a small team needs one.** The scope boundary names "five transports (terminal, Telegram, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp)" and five transport modules [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:45] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:62]. For a small team, the adapter contract plus the terminal transport plus Telegram — the one transport that long-polls and needs no public URL — proves the design; Slack, Signal and WhatsApp add three wire protocols, three token shapes and three test suites in the same phase. **Exact edit**: split 011 into 011a (adapter contract, link, lockout, approval index, queue, terminal and Telegram) and 011b (Slack, Signal, WhatsApp), or mark the three transports as follow-ups in the phase's scope boundary with their modules moved to a later packet.
**The ranked cut list, largest saving first.** Six surfaces can be cut or shrunk without losing a capability the eleven phases promise. Ranked by the work removed:

**P1 — 001's notice criterion cannot pass if 001 takes its own documented fallback.** AC-006 requires that `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` name both OpenBot source files [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/acceptance-criteria.md:59], and REQ-006 says the same [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:153].
